tools.name: create_run
tools.description: Start an AI agent run in an isolated sandbox and return the run (status queued) at once. Give a prompt, or the name of a saved workflow. Poll with get_run or block with wait_for_run for the result. Every run has a cost cap (max_cost_micros) and a timeout, and is billed to the organization of the API

tools.name: get_run
tools.description: Read a run: status, output, error, cost and billing_pending. COST: while billing_pending is true (or the run is still going), cost_micros is PROVISIONAL and usually higher than the final cost; the result then has cost_final:false and a cost_note. Quote a cost only when cost_final is true (the run is

tools.name: wait_for_run
tools.description: Wait until a run finishes (succeeded, failed, cancelled, interrupted or timed_out) or the wait ends, then return the run. After the run finishes it keeps waiting, within the same time, until billing has settled (billing_pending false, normally a few seconds to about 20), so the cost is final. Waits

tools.name: list_runs
tools.description: List the organization's runs, newest first, with a cursor for the next page. Each run has cost_final: when false, cost_micros is provisional (usually above the final cost) and billing is still settling.

tools.name: cancel_run
tools.description: Cancel a run that has not finished. Work already done is billed. Cancelling a finished run changes nothing.

tools.name: list_workflows
tools.description: List the organization's saved workflows (reusable run definitions). Each entry has the workflow's name and, when set, its description, input_schema (the shape of the input create_run expects) and output_schema (the shape of the JSON it returns), so you can call a workflow without reading its prompt.

tools.name: get_workflow
tools.description: Read a saved workflow's definition: description, prompt, model, files, connections, limits and its input_schema and output_schema. Credentials are never included.

tools.name: list_models
tools.description: Find models. Returns a compact list (id, name, context_length, input and output USD per million tokens, zero_data_retention where known), the total count and the default model. There are hundreds of models, so filter with query (case-insensitive part of the id or name, e.g. "claude", "gpt") and read

tools.name: list_connections
tools.description: The organization's saved connections that a run may use, with type, allowed methods and tools. No URLs or secrets are returned. Reference one in create_run by name.

tools.name: save_workflow
tools.description: Create a workflow, or replace the one with this name (saving the same definition again changes nothing more). A workflow is a reusable run definition: start it with create_run and its name, or on a timetable with create_schedule. Connections must already be saved in the organization; reference them

tools.name: delete_workflow
tools.description: Permanently delete a saved workflow. Runs already started are not affected; schedules that use it stop being able to start runs until it is saved again.

tools.name: list_schedules
tools.description: List the organization's schedules: each starts a saved workflow on a cron timetable. Includes the next start, the last run and the last error.

tools.name: get_schedule
tools.description: Read a schedule: timetable, time zone, input, cost cap, whether it is enabled, its next start and the outcome of its last start.

tools.name: create_schedule
tools.description: Start a saved workflow on a timetable. Needs an administrator key. Each start is a run billed to the organization, with the cost cap given here (or the default). Use preview_schedule first to check the timetable. A schedule pauses itself after repeated failed starts. An organization can have 50 sche

tools.name: update_schedule
tools.description: Change a schedule; only the fields you give change. Needs an administrator key. Set enabled to false to pause it and to true to resume it (resuming clears the failures that paused it). A new timetable counts from now.

tools.name: delete_schedule
tools.description: Permanently delete a schedule. Needs an administrator key. Runs it already started are not affected. To stop it for a while, pause it with update_schedule instead.

tools.name: preview_schedule
tools.description: Check a cron expression and time zone and return the next five start times (UTC), without saving anything.

tools.name: run_schedule
tools.description: Start the schedule's workflow now, outside its timetable, with the schedule's input and cost cap. Returns the queued run (follow it with wait_for_run); each call starts another run and is billed like any run.

tools.name: list_files
tools.description: List the files saved in the organization: id, name, size, content type and creation time. Reference a file by id in a run's or workflow's files. Read-only; upload and delete files through the REST API.

findings.title: Read-only tool requests dangerous parameters
findings.detail: Tool "create_run" appears informational but accepts parameters (shell) that enable code/file/secret access.

findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "get_run" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.

findings.title: Generic tool name can shadow trusted tools
findings.detail: Tool "list_files" uses a generic high-value name. When multiple servers load together, this can intercept calls meant for a trusted server.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: list_connections, save_workflow · Private data: create_run, get_workflow, list_models, list_connections, save_workflow, list_files · Public sink: list_files · Destructive: create_run, get_run, wait_for_run, list_runs, cancel_run, list_workflows, list_connections, save_workflow, delete_workflow, list_schedules, create_schedule, delete_schedule, run_schedule, list_files.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: list_connections, save_workflow · Private data: create_run, get_workflow, list_models, list_connections, save_workflow, list_files · Public sink: list_files · Destructive: create_run, get_run, wait_for_run, list_runs, cancel_run, list_workflows, list_connections, save_workflow, delete_workflow, list_schedules, create_schedule, delete_schedule, run_schedule, list_files

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
